name: TikTok
summary: TikTok OAuth requires a formal app review before any external user can connect. Developers can test immediately in Sandbox mode, but production launch requires domain ownership verification, product and scope justifications, and a recorded demo video showing the full login flow.

verdict.label: Hard
verdict.approvalWait: Not published (TikTok official docs do not state expected app review turn-around times)

decideFirst.question: Will you test initially in Sandbox mode or prepare directly for Production?
decideFirst.guidance: Use Sandbox mode to test OAuth flows instantly without waiting for app review. Switch to Production mode and submit for review when you are ready to allow external users to log in.

evidence.note: TikTok provides a Sandbox mode that bypasses app review for testing.

decideFirst.question: What target platform are you building for (Web, iOS, Android, or Desktop)?
decideFirst.guidance: Redirect URI rules and PKCE requirements vary by platform. Desktop requires PKCE and loopback URIs (`localhost`). Mobile platforms use TikTok OpenSDK with Universal Links (iOS) or App Links (Android). Web requires static HTTPS URIs with no query parameters.

decideFirst.question: What permissions beyond basic user identity (`user.info.basic`) do you need?
decideFirst.guidance: Basic profile info (`user.info.basic`) is the default baseline. Requesting higher-tier products like Content Posting API or Data Portability requires explicit pre-approval during app review and extra URL verification steps.

phases.name: 1 · Developer Setup & Sandbox Testing
phases.goal: Register your application, configure Login Kit redirect URIs, and test the authorization flow in Sandbox mode.

steps.title: Create a Developer Account & Organization
steps.detail: Sign up for a TikTok developer account. Create or join an Organization on TikTok for Developers to ensure shared app management across your team.

steps.title: Register a New App
steps.detail: In the Manage Apps console, click 'Connect an app', assign ownership to your Organization, and populate basic details including App Name, Icon (1024x1024), Category, and Description.

steps.title: Add Login Kit & Configure Redirect URIs
steps.detail: Add the Login Kit product to your app. Configure static HTTPS redirect URIs (up to 10 URIs, max 512 characters each, no query parameters or fragments).

steps.title: Test Authorization Flow in Sandbox
steps.detail: Toggle your app to Sandbox mode. Implement authorization calls pointing to `https://www.tiktok.com/v2/auth/authorize/` with `client_key`, `scope`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, and `response_type=code`. Verify access token exchange on your backend.

phases.name: 2 · Domain Ownership & Production Review Submission
phases.goal: Verify ownership of your site domains and submit your application for TikTok app review.

steps.title: Verify Domain / URL Properties
steps.detail: Click 'URL properties' in the developer console. Verify ownership of your Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL, and Web/Desktop URLs by uploading a signature file to your server or verifying domain prefixes.

steps.title: Record Demo Video of OAuth Integration
steps.detail: Record a demo video (1 to 5 videos, up to 50 MB each) demonstrating the complete end-to-end authorization flow, scope usage, and features within your app.

steps.title: Submit Production App for Review
steps.detail: Fill out detailed justifications explaining how each requested product and scope is used. Click 'Submit for review' under Production mode.

phases.name: 3 · Review Monitoring & Production Release
phases.goal: Handle review feedback and go live to allow external TikTok users to authorize your integration.

steps.title: Monitor App Review Status
steps.detail: Track app status in the portal (Draft -> In Review -> Live / Not Approved). If recalled or requested by TikTok reviewers, address comments and resubmit.

steps.title: Handle App Revisions
steps.detail: Once live, any future updates to products or scopes require creating a draft revision while keeping the current live version active.

requirements.note: Registering apps under an Organization allows collaborative sandbox testing and shared management.
Apps created after September 9, 2024 must verify Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and Web domain URLs via signature file upload or domain prefix verification.
Must show the end-to-end integration flow (1-5 files, max 50 MB per video).
Must be absolute, static (no query parameters or hash fragments), max 512 characters, starting with https://.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI rejected during portal setup
blockers.cause: The URI contains query parameters, fragment identifiers (#), is non-HTTPS (for web), or exceeds 512 characters.
blockers.fix: Provide a clean, static, absolute HTTPS URL without query strings (e.g. `https://example.com/auth/callback`).

blockers.symptom: User callback returns an `error` query parameter
blockers.cause: The user is ineligible for third-party TikTok login or authorization in their region/account type.
blockers.fix: Handle the `error` and `error_description` fields gracefully in your callback handler and display a user-friendly error message.

nuances.title: PKCE Enforcement by Platform
nuances.detail: PKCE (code_verifier and S256 code_challenge) is mandatory for Desktop, iOS, and Android applications. Web client integrations use confidential backend secrets and CSRF state parameters instead.

nuances.title: Strict Redirect URI Format Restrictions
nuances.detail: Web redirect URIs cannot contain query strings (`?id=1`) or fragments (`#100`). Each app allows a maximum of 10 static redirect URIs.

nuances.title: Production App Revisions
nuances.detail: When modifying settings or scopes on an already approved 'Live' app, TikTok creates a 'Draft' revision. Your existing live version remains operational while the draft is submitted for review.
